column3: Declared HTTP routes not reached by a completed request are listed in sorted order, capped at 100; the agent view keeps eight and counts omissions. Any journal eviction refuses classification because sharpit has no run-wide route aggregates.
Framework handlers use the fastapi and starlette module prefixes; opaque mounts, custom routes, WebSockets and Python path catch-alls are excluded.
Python converter syntax remains unchanged on both declared paths and captured labels, rather than canonicalising only the declared path.

Plain Starlette routes are omitted and counted in a limitation because captured templates are unavailable on FastAPI and older Starlette releases. A request they answer leaves the other declared routes classified.
A capture suspension during the run refuses classification even after resume; the boundary is recorded at hook transitions, without per-request bookkeeping.
METADATA_ONLY refuses classification because masked request identifiers and labels cannot prove route exercise.
Secret-looking route literals may be listed despite having been called when their captured label is masked; a limitation states this and a regression test pins it.
An HTTP 404 without a captured route template never marks a declared route exercised, including a Host route rejected by its host condition.

A completed non-404 HTTP request with an explicitly absent route template refuses classification only when its method and path could belong to a listed declared FastAPI route, because included FastAPI routers can lose their prefix at capture, or when its path is masked and cannot be matched. Other template-less traffic (a CORS preflight, a static file, a slash redirect, a plain Starlette route, an opaque mount) is ignored, as an unmatched 404 is, and its path label never marks a declared route exercised.

BootUI v2.5.0 does not mask the notExercised list. sharpit masks each declared route label at output through the service masker because the safety model requires secrets masked before every output, including HTTP and CLI/MCP agent views.
